bull.b: The $519M cash balance and low leverage provide meaningful funding visibility for the lead MASH program. Management expects the existing runway to support PERFORMA through its 52-week readout, reducing near-term financing pressure while pivotal development advances.

bull.t: Promising AUD clinical efficacy and biomarker results
bull.b: RECLAIM produced positive results across drinking behavior, validated risk-level endpoints, and the objective PEth biomarker. This breadth of evidence strengthens pemvidutide’s potential differentiation in AUD and supports regulatory discussions for a future pivotal program.

bull.t: Global Phase III MASH program initiated
bull.b: Starting a large global Phase III trial represents a material transition toward late-stage validation of pemvidutide in MASH. Broad site coverage and defined enrollment and readout milestones create a clearer development path for the company’s lead asset.

bear.t: No meaningful commercial revenue and persistent losses
bear.b: Altimmune remains dependent on financing rather than product sales because it has no approved commercialized drug. Large recurring losses and substantial cash burn consume capital ahead of potential approval, limiting financial self-sufficiency and increasing execution sensitivity.

bear.t: Current runway excludes a potential AUD Phase III
bear.b: The company may need royalties, debt, or strategic partnerships to advance AUD into Phase III, and management said those sources are not yet secured. This creates funding and execution uncertainty around expanding the pipeline beyond the currently financed MASH program.

bear.t: Tolerability monitoring and competitive enrollment risk
bear.b: GI-related discontinuations require further analysis because tolerability can affect adherence, trial completion, and eventual labeling. At the same time, competing MASH studies may pressure enrollment speed and costs, complicating execution of the lead Phase III program.
